# Personal Bunkers
Use a bunker hatch and choose Enter my room to enter your character's private quarters, or Enter cryo to rest as usual. Each character has a separate room, saved on this server. Renaming your character keeps their room; deleting the character does not transfer it to a new character.
Your room starts with a small concrete interior, a roof, breathable air, and a lit exit ladder. Bring furniture and decorations to make it your own. Use the ladder to return to the hatch you entered through. Anything you are dragging follows you through the hatch and ladder.
Rooms save once when the last occupant leaves. Empty rooms unload after a short grace period without saving a second time. A final safety save still runs at round end or normal server shutdown. There is no repeating autosave while you are inside. Furniture, decorations, and items inside containers are saved. Players, bodies, and everything they are wearing or carrying are excluded. An occupied room stays loaded. If you enter critical condition or go SSD inside, your body and belongings are returned to the entrance hatch. The room saves when empty, just as if you had left through the ladder. Ghosts are returned to the hatch when no living, awake player remains inside, so observers cannot keep an abandoned room loaded.
Dispenser source bottles, inserted beakers, and their remaining chemicals are preserved when your room reloads. Chemistry-set buffers do not trigger reactions when the room reloads; use a suitable reaction container to mix chemicals. Shelves can be opened normally after returning.
## Visiting another bunker
Choose Join Another at a bunker hatch to see occupied bunkers. Select Request access and stay by the hatch while the owner answers. Approval takes you to the room entrance. The ladder returns you to the hatch you used to request the visit.
## Save failures
If a save fails, an empty room still unloads after its normal grace period rather than repeatedly retrying. Its last successful save is retained, but changes since that save may be lost.
## Display weapons and armor
Ammo boxes and magazines left in the saved room become decorative: they still look filled but cannot hold or supply ammunition. IDs become decorative and lose access, identification and messaging functionality.
Super and ultra stim liquids left in the room become normal stim liquid when saved, keeping the same volume and container names. Mail and parcels are deleted on save. The mail machine stays.
Toolboxes are excluded from decorative weapon conversion and remain usable storage after saving.
Weapons left in the room become permanent decorations after the last occupant leaves, even inside containers. Weapons remain functional while someone is inside. Guns lose their loaded ammunition and cannot shoot or be reloaded. Melee weapons lose their original damage and deal only 1 blunt. Taking a display weapon out of the room does not restore it.
Armor and helmets left behind also become permanent decorations, including armor worn by a mannequin or stored inside a container. Decorative armor provides no damage, stamina, reflection, explosion, or environmental protection. Picking it up or reloading the room does not restore its protection. Armor you are wearing or carrying out remains functional.
Build a mannequin from the G menu under Furniture using 5 wood planks. Open its inventory to dress it in clothing and armor. A screwdriver dismantles it and returns its clothing and materials.
Keep functional weapons and armor on your person. Your equipped and carried items, including the contents of your bags, are excluded from room saves and display conversion.
## Furnishing your room
Use the G menu to craft a weapon plaque (2 wood planks), a shower (3 steel), a bunker wall light (2 steel), carpet squares in every available color (2 cloth each), and curtains in every available color (2 cloth each). Colored light tubes cost 2 glass each. Bunker wall lights work without electrical wiring but still need an intact tube; changing the tube changes the light color.
Crafted curtains have no locks or keys. Plaques and bunker wall lights can be mounted directly on bunker walls.
Use a weapon on a plaque to display that weapon, then use an empty hand to remove it. Plaques hold one weapon of any size. Mounted weapons still follow the bunker display conversion rules when the last occupant leaves. Empty the plaque or remove a light's tube before dismantling its fixture with a screwdriver. ## Bunker PCs
Open Bunker PCs under Survival in this guidebook for computer crafting, apps, records, messaging, profiles, passcodes, and holotape games.
